implementation: Installed stable std::alloc::GlobalAlloc hook with atomic shared counters, standard containers, and fallible reservation APIs; no allocator-api2 or per-buffer allocator registration.
scope: Declarative driver construction/encoding only; no terminal-plan execution or commit. Rust/RSS measurements include local reference-engine work and caller query construction. Global-allocator builds also track caller diagnostics, so exact per-container cleanup baselines do not apply. Allocation aborts in pressure probes are recoverability gaps, not successful error returns. A sampled ratio is not allocation-stack attribution.

source.source_digest_algorithm: SHA256 of sorted relative UTF-8 path, NUL, file bytes, NUL for each source_input_files entry.
source.source_digest_note: After executable validation, peak/reset documentation and Python abort classification were tightened. Saved gap receipts and fresh smoke probes confirm the same classification; measured Rust executable code is unchanged.

allocator_behavior.reservation: Atomic compare-and-swap checks overflow and the limit before calling the backing allocator.
allocator_behavior.release: Atomic fetch_sub after backing deallocation; allocation failure rolls back its reservation.
allocator_behavior.reallocation: Reserve complete replacement while old bytes remain charged, delegate to backing realloc, then release old bytes on success or roll back replacement on failure.
allocator_behavior.configuration: Allocation-free atomic reader/writer gate excludes reservations during limit changes, usage snapshots, and peak resets; backing calls and frees hold no gate.

normal_kernel_validation.compiler_diagnostic_test: Separated compiler-message test uses its expected Rust 1.100 toolchain; no stderr snapshots overwritten.
normal_kernel_validation.generated_c_actual_cdylib: Two unlimited and two 64-MiB lifecycle passes, zero-headroom write-state encoding returns memory error 59 and retries after clearing the limit, foreign pthread releases retained bytes at zero extra headroom, stable retained baseline after full release.

peak_measurement_notes: One measured operation per query, concurrency 1, tracking enabled and limit disabled. Includes fixed canonical schemas, caller/harness, and local Rust reference-engine allocations.
Rust and reservation peaks reset after warmup. RSS is process high-water and includes startup/warmup. Independent peaks need not coincide.
Reservation peaks can exceed actual requested Rust heap due to conservative old-plus-new realloc accounting, including in-place growth.
Current validation contains no new DHAT allocation-stack profiles. Historical profiles in RESULTS.json and GLOBAL_ALLOC_VALIDATION.json retain their original provenance.

allocation_fault_survey.coverage_note: One-shot global fault sequences stop at the first infallible gap; ordinal coverage is not exhaustive.

limitations: Recoverability is incomplete: infallible Arc/Box/container, dependency, engine, and caller allocations may abort when the global hook rejects a request.
Pressure probes span Kernel, caller construction, and the local reference engine. Abort counts are not attributed exclusively to Kernel.
Recovery gaps are explicitly recorded with --record-infallible-gaps; default strict runs fail on these aborts. Unlimited/fit failures and unexpected errors still fail either mode.

The limit bounds requested Rust reservations through this allocator domain, not whole-process native memory or RSS. Direct libc/C++, foreign engine storage, mappings, stacks, allocator overhead, and retained pages are outside requested-layout accounting.
Current serial stage observations agree exactly with an independent requested-Rust-byte tracker. This is not a new simultaneous-peak allocation-stack attribution or an RSS coverage fraction.
Terminal metadata-plan execution and declarative commit are not exercised by this lifecycle.
Correctness-run timings with one repetition cannot establish p99.9 latency or performance regressions.
superseded_reason: Process-global rejection exposed ordinary infallible allocations to abort. Replaced by an explicit opt-in Allocator backend with Kernel MSRV 1.95 and budgeting/FFI MSRV 1.100.
